liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Reviewer calls this song a thing of beauty [21]
- **Passenger** (1 other source): Start of the song is clipped and the whole song sounds muffled [4]
- Reviewer believes Rosalie McFall, Dark Hollow and To Lay Me Down are the Reckoning versions [14]
- Reviewer especially enjoys the piano and this song [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **Franken And Davis**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **Deep Elem Blues**: back after 160 archived shows (687 days) [22]
- **Franken And Davis**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **Franken And Davis**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-10-04.151437.sbd.1st-gen.miller.t.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 37 songs; 268 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: A little hissy, but really good once the music gets going [1]
- **gd1980-10-04.151265.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 37 songs; 268 min [2]. Said about its sound: A little hissy, but really good once the music gets going [2]
- **gd80-10-04.sbd.blanchard.14989.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 34 songs; 206 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [3]
- **gd1980-10-04.164898.electric.aud.gale.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 156 min [4]
- **gd80-10-04.sbd.bertha-ashley.19147.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 67 min; rated 4.67/5 by 12 [8]. Said about its sound: Crisp sound; audible audience clapping when slides appeared, such as Bob clowning around with Pig in the Haight; Bobby is a bit loud early, bass drum is up, and Phil's monitor balance comes off low [14][19]

## Around the show

- Barnyard-style stage set; slides spanning the band's whole career were projected during playing, such as Jerry on a camel in Egypt [14]
- Media player labeled Deep Elem Blues as Bertha, with a running time of 4:20 [19]
- Reviewer attended the weekend shows and rates the acoustic set on the 11th as the best one [10]
- Reviewer says it has 31 songs, not counting Drums and Space, making for a remarkable setlist [11]
- Audio is better on other recordings from this run; suggests starting with the set a week later [19]
- Deal and Feel Like A Stranger from this show appear on the compilation Dead Set, drawn from Sept. and Oct. 1980 [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-10-04.151437.sbd.1st-gen.miller.t.flac16**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 24, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550) > Cassette (Sony TC-D5M/TDK SA-C90) [1]. Also: First-generation soundboard, converted from the 24-bit source 151265 to 16-bit at 44.1 kHz [1]
- **gd1980-10-04.151265.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 24, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550) > Cassette (Sony TC-D5M/TDK SA-C90) [2]
- **gd80-10-04.sbd.blanchard.14989.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Complete soundboard, transferred through an unknown generation to CDR, then EAC, then Cool Edit with minor cleanup [3]
- **gd1980-10-04.164898.electric.aud.gale.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Unknown from the collection of Dan Gale; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Low Gen audience recording; unknown equipment, from the Dan Gale collection [4]
- **gd80-10-04.sbd.bertha-ashley.19147.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [8]
